newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cbank says policy aims at soft landing.
newsitem.headline: Czech cbank says policy aims at soft landing.

text.p: Czech National Bank governor Josef Tosovsky said on Friday the bank's monetary policy was aimed at achieving a "soft landing" for interest rates.

"We are using the soft landing," Tosovsky told reporters at a meeting of the Czech-German chamber of commerce and industry. Asked if that meant interest rates would be lowered only gradually, he said, "Yes, there was an example of that today."
The central bank set a one-week reverse repo tender at a maximum rate of 22 percent, down from 29 percent at the last one-week tender.
The bank raised rates sharply in recent weeks in a failed attempt to protect the crown from a wave of speculative selling.
The bank eventually floated the crown, previously fixed against a mark/dollar basket, on May 27 and rates have gradually been falling.
The repo rate peaked at 75 percent and many analysts are awaiting a lowering of the Lombard rate from its current 50 percent.
An IMF mission to Prague called on Thursday on Czech authorities to lower rates only slowly, saying monetary policy should not permit "an undesirable weakening of the crown exchange rate".
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, who delivered a speech to the chamber meeting, complimented Tosovsky, calling him a "real expert".
Czech central bank board member Ludek Niedermayer earlier told a news conference developments in the crown's exchange rate in recent days had been positive.
"We see the development of the crown over the past few days as positive. The rate has been steady at around 18.5 to the Deutsche mark and stable," he said.
The crown stood at 18.519 to the mark at 1320 GMT.
